Tensor Analysis – Practical 3 Information: • Please make sure to complete all exercises before the next lecture. • The exercises marked with [See lecture] were solved in class. • The exercises are not organised by difficulty. 3.1 [See lecture] Use the transformation law to show that ∇ is a vector. 3.2 [See lecture] Let f be a scalar field. Show that ∇ · (∇f ) is is a scalar using the transformation law. 3.3 Use the transformation law and the fact that ∇ and w are vectors to show that w · ∇ is a scalar. 3.4 Consider Lij = ∂x′ i ∂xj . Show that ∂Lij ∂x′ i = 0. 3.5 Suppose e1, e2, e3 are basis vectors for a Cartesian coordinate system, and let e′ 1, e′ 2, e′ 3 be the images of e1, e2, e3 under a rotation. For each i, let ei = ai1e ′ 1 + ai2e ′ 2 + ai3e ′ 3 be the expansion for ei in terms of e′ j. Find expressions for the aij’s in terms of ei and e′ j. 3.6 Let u be the vector field defined by u = h(r)r, where h(r) is an arbitrary differentiable function, and r is the position vector r = (x1, x2, x3) with r = |r|. Show, using suffix notation, that ∇ × u = 0. [Hint: Exercise 2.8 can help you here: ∇h(r) = h′(r)r/r.] 3.7 Show that ∇ · ∇2u = ∇2∇ · u in two ways: (1) directly using suffix notation; (2) first using ∇2u = ∇(∇ · u) − ∇ × (∇ × u) from the lectures, and then using suffix notation. 1
